paragraphs: On Thursday, the Explorers met in the school library after lunch. Teacher Kim put a big map of the old town on the table. "On Saturday, we are going sightseeing in the old town," she said. "Each of you has a job, so please listen." Lily had to find the old sundial for a science page on the blog. Mia had to take photos, and Leo had to draw the old gate. May had to talk to a woman in a shop, but she felt shy. "Don't be late on Saturday!" said Teacher Kim.

On Saturday morning, the club met at the bus stop near the old town. Tom and Ben came to help. Tom carried the water bottles. The sun was hot, but the old street was cool under the trees. They walked past wooden houses and a small market. May stopped at a shop. "Is there a sundial here?" she asked a woman. "Yes, it is in the square," said the woman, "but today there is a dance show." May was happy, so she did not feel shy now.

In the square, many people stood around a young dancer. She wore a silver ring. She danced to slow music. Mia took ten photos, but Lily could not see the sundial. "There are too many people," said Lily. "Let's wait until the music stops," said Teacher Kim. Leo drew the dancer in his notebook, so he was not bored.

When the music stopped, the dancer looked at her hand. "Oh no, my silver ring is gone!" she said. The children looked on the ground, but they could not see it. Lily saw the sundial in the middle of the square. A red bike stood against it. Ben moved the bike, and something small and silver lay in the grass. "Is this your ring?" asked Lily. "Yes, it is!" said the dancer with a big smile. "Now you can see the sundial," said Teacher Kim. "The sun makes a shadow, and the shadow shows the time." "That is science, too," said Lily. "The shadow is on the ten, and my watch says ten, too," said Ben.

In the evening, Lily wrote the blog page. Mia sent her the photos. Lily also wrote to Grace, her friend in Singapore. They keep in contact by email. She told Grace about the ring. Grace wrote back, "Please send more photos!" It was a good Saturday, and Lily smiled.
